title: Why Paying Cash for a Car Costs You More

beats.say: You think paying cash for a car saves you money, but the actual math on a $25,000 purchase proves you might be richer keeping the cash.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of car keys resting on dark wet asphalt under a single sodium light.

beats.say: It feels incredible to own a vehicle outright with zero debt hanging over your head.
beats.visual: Low angle of a sleek sedan parked alone in an empty multi-story concrete parking garage at night.

beats.say: Most people assume avoiding interest always wins.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking away down a long, fog-cut highway under cold fluorescent overheads.

beats.say: So why do math-driven buyers choose a 5% loan instead?
beats.visual: High angle shot of wet traffic tails cutting red lines through a dark city street.

beats.say: A 5-year, $25,000 loan at 5% interest costs about $3,300 over the term.
beats.visual: Close-up of a hand tapping a dark dashboard with only the glowing speedometer visible.

beats.say: Where does that leave the actual cash you started with?
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary bridge tower fading into heavy gray fog at dawn.

beats.say: If you keep that $25,000 invested at 8% a year, it grows much faster than the loan eats.
beats.visual: Macro shot of cold morning condensation rolling down a tinted car window.

beats.say: At 8% a year, that lump sum compounds to over $36,000 in five years.
beats.visual: Sodium light reflecting off the wet hood of a parked car in an empty alleyway.

beats.say: Subtract the loan cost and the interest, and you are roughly $8,000 ahead.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a single commuter standing at the edge of an empty train platform at blue hour.

beats.say: As long as your monthly cash flow covers the payment, your lump sum out-earns the debt.
beats.visual: Low angle shot looking up past concrete bridge pillars into a dark, overcast sky.

beats.say: That is the quiet math behind modern leverage.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of rubber tires gripping wet asphalt under cold sodium lights.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Fade to a dark, minimalist slate with a single sharp practical light reflecting off wet pavement.
